commits.message:
feat: enable cli-proxy for smoke-services and firewall-issue-dispatcher (#1862)

* feat: enable cli-proxy for smoke-services and firewall-issue-dispatcher

Enable the cli-proxy feature for two Copilot-engine workflows that
heavily use the GitHub MCP server:

- smoke-services: I/O ratio 375:1, $0.89/run avg
- firewall-issue-dispatcher: I/O ratio 396:1, $0.51/run avg

The cli-proxy replaces MCP GitHub tool calls with gh CLI commands
via bash, avoiding the large MCP tool schemas that inflate context
on every turn. This should significantly reduce input token usage.

Both workflows compiled with gh-aw v0.67.4.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: add firewall-issue-dispatcher to post-processing targets

The firewall-issue-dispatcher lock file was using --image-tag/--skip-pull
which requires the cli-proxy image to be published to GHCR. Since the
cli-proxy image hasn't been released yet, the container failed to start
with 'No such image: ghcr.io/github/gh-aw-firewall/cli-proxy:0.25.18'.

Fix: Add firewall-issue-dispatcher.lock.yml to the post-processing
script's target list so it gets --build-local (builds from source).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* api-proxy: log billing/quota response headers and X-Initiator sent

Extract X-Quota-Snapshot-* headers (PRU entitlement, overage, remaining)
and rate-limit headers from upstream CAPI responses. Include them in:
- request_complete structured log (for real-time visibility)
- token-usage JSONL records (for offline billing analysis)

Also logs the X-Initiator value that was sent on the request so operators
can correlate billing treatment with initiator tagging.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* schemas: add x_initiator and billing fields to token-usage schema

Document the new optional fields added to token-usage.jsonl records:
- x_initiator: the X-Initiator header value sent (agent/user)
- billing: parsed X-Quota-Snapshot-* and X-RateLimit-* response headers

These fields enable offline analysis of PRU billing behavior.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ci): increase one-shot-token test timeouts for Docker build

The container-mode tests use buildLocal: true which triggers a full
Docker image build. On CI without cached layers, the first 2-3 tests
hit the 60s AWF timeout (execa kills process → exit code -1) because
Docker build alone takes ~55-60s.

- AWF timeout: 60000 → 180000ms (3 minutes)
- Jest timeout: 120000 → 240000ms (4 minutes)

The chroot-mode tests pass quickly (14s) because images are already
built by then.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ci): make audit artifacts world-readable to prevent EACCES in gh-aw post-run

The gh-aw post-run audit step runs as the 'runner' user but AWF creates
audit files as root with mode 0600. When AWF cleanup is interrupted
(SIGKILL from timeout), the chmod a+rX never runs, leaving files
unreadable and causing:

  EACCES: permission denied, stat 'docker-compose.redacted.yml'

Fix: Create audit files with mode 0644 (dir 0755) from the start. These
files contain no secrets — squid.conf has only domain ACLs, compose is
redacted, and policy-manifest is just firewall rules.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ci): increase smoke workflow timeouts from 5 to 15 minutes

With --build-local, Docker image builds take 7+ minutes on cold cache
(no layer cache on CI runners). The 5-minute step timeout causes the
Copilot CLI execution step to be killed before the agent even starts.

Increase timeout-minutes from 5 to 15 in:
- smoke-copilot-byok (md + lock)
- smoke-copilot (md + lock)
- smoke-gemini (md only, lock was already 15)

fix: firewall-issue-dispatcher always skipping activation (#6648)

* fix: firewall-issue-dispatcher always skipping activation

The top-level if condition (needs['fetch-awf-issues'].result == 'success')
was compiled onto the activation job, which does not declare fetch-awf-issues
as a dependency. The expression evaluated to empty, so activation was always
skipped, cascading skips to fetch-awf-issues and the agent job.

Remove the redundant top-level if; the agent job already declares
needs: fetch-awf-issues, so a failed fetch skips the agent automatically.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 668c3d21-8ed5-4f02-aed0-132e26be9cb8

* fix: authenticate fetch-awf-issues job with GITHUB_TOKEN

The compiled fetch-awf-issues job ran 'gh api graphql' with no token, so it
would fail authentication before producing the artifact, skipping the agent.

The step's GH_TOKEN env was silently dropped at compile time: gh-aw rewrites
'${{ runner.temp }}' inside run: blocks into an injected GH_AW_RUNNER_TEMP env
map, which replaced the user-provided env. Switch the run script to the
built-in $RUNNER_TEMP so no env injection occurs, and set
GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} (sufficient for this public cross-repo
issue read). Recompiled the lock file.

Co-authored-by: Copilot App <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 668c3d21-8ed5-4f02-aed0-132e26be9cb8

* fix: use GH_AW_CROSS_REPO_PAT for fetch-awf-issues auth

Reading issues from github/gh-aw requires the cross-repo PAT, not the
repo-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN. Now that the run script uses $RUNNER_TEMP (avoiding
the env-injection that previously dropped the token), the PAT is preserved in
the compiled lock file.
